Subject: Recap: Private hosting requirements & next steps (Valencia Health)

Hi Sophie / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. I wanted to capture the key points we discussed and confirm next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. I’ve included Priyom (solutions engineering) and Evelyn (customer success) to own technical follow-ups and onboarding planning.

Summary of pain & goals
- Regulatory driver: Valencia needs an air-gapped or private VPC deployment for the new patient-facing routing engine because of regional PHI handling rules and upcoming audits.
- Primary goals: keep latency under 220ms P95 for inference, guarantee data never leaves the customer VPC, and provide audit logs for all inference requests for 12+ months.
- Current blockers: restrictive egress rules in Valencia’s environment, mandatory on-prem HSM for key material, and procurement requiring SOC2-type artifacts before PO.

Technical constraints discussed
- Networking: no outbound internet from the subnet running the model. They will allow tightly scoped egress to Redwood-managed endpoints only via a private peering or VPC endpoint.
- Auth/KMS: customer requires KMS/HSM integration (HSM on-prem) for root keys; we can support bring-your-own-key with limited surface area.
- Data residency: all inference logs and cache must be stored in Valencia’s tenancy/region. Temporary KV cache must not persist beyond configured TTL and must be encrypted at rest.
- Air-gap expectations: customer expects a staged approach: 1) Private VPC with strict peering and limited egress, 2) Optional on-prem bundle for later phases if audits demand fully isolated deployment.

Attachments
- I’ve attached a short checklist: valencia_network_prereq.pdf (network ports, IPs, peering requirements) and our security questionnaire answers: valencia_security_answers.xlsx.

Immediate next steps and owners
1) Priyom: run a feasibility check on a private VPC + HSM integration and propose a minimal-network architecture diagram by Thu, 2026-08-05. (Action: produce an annotated diagram and list of required CIDRs/ports)
2) Evelyn: draft a high-level SOW and estimated timeline for a pilot (4–6 weeks) and a baseline pricing range for Dedicated or Private options by Fri, 2026-08-06.
3) Sophie/Tom: confirm whether procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence or specific control reports and share the primary procurement contact. (Action: reply to this thread)
4) Karthik: prepare a concise PoC plan (scope: 1 model, 5k req/day baseline) and share the acceptance criteria and success metrics.

Proposed PoC milestones (brief)
- Week 0: network prep and account connectivity
- Week 1–2: deploy model to private environment and validate basic requests
- Week 3: performance tuning and KV/cache configuration
- Week 4: acceptance testing and success metric verification

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks again — we’ll prioritize the feasibility diagram and the SOW drafts so procurement has what it needs.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Private hosting requirements & next steps (Valencia Health)

Karthik — thanks for the recap, that looks accurate. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: we do need SOC2 Type II evidence and a copy of the last penetration test report. If Redwood can provide a SOC2 report and a contact for security evaluation, that will speed procurement.
- Networking nuance: our security team will not allow direct peering to third-party-managed VPCs; we need either a customer-managed transit VPC (we host the transit) or a VPN into our private subnet. In short, we can support cross-account peering only if clear egress controls are enforced and there is no route to public internet.
- HSM detail: our on-prem HSM team prefers the HSM to be behind an internal firewall with only a single outbound tunnel to the Redwood key proxy; we need to validate latency and handshake options.

Action items for our side:
- I will introduce our procurement lead (procure@valenciahealth.com) and our security architect (s.arch@valenciahealth.com) on the next reply.
- We’ll confirm whether the pilot can run in a customer-managed subnet or if we must do a VPN. Expect that answer by 2026-08-04 EOD.

Thanks,
Tom
Sr. Engineering Manager — Platform Integrations
Valencia Health

Thanks, Karthik. I’ll own the feasibility assessment. Quick notes from my side after an initial review of your network checklist:
- We can support a customer-managed transit VPC model: Redwood nodes run in your AWS account under a dedicated subnet (we deploy an agentless control plane into your VPC) OR we can set up an AWS PrivateLink endpoint that terminates into a Redwood-managed environment with strict ACLs. Both approaches can meet the no-public-egress requirement with the right config.
- For HSM: we’ll need a short PKI exchange and a firewall rule allowing calls to our key-proxy. If the HSM is strictly air-gapped we can also support an offline key-loading process for root keys and then use a signed cert rotation path for day-to-day operations.
- Latency: with dedicated placement in your region and optimized kernel selection we expect to meet the 220ms P95 target for short prompts; we will validate with a small perf run during PoC.

Deliverables I’ll provide by Thu, 2026-08-05 EOD:
1) Annotated network diagram (CIDRs, peering/VPN options)
2) Short table of inbound/outbound ports and IPs required
3) HSM integration options and a recommended sequence for key material exchange
4) Rough perf estimate and PoC validation plan

I’ll attach the diagram to this thread when ready.

—Priyom
